trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum, so it pops automatically once the other 54 trophies are yours — there is no separate task to complete. Work through the story chapters first, then sweep the side content: stranger strands, collectibles, activities and the big grinds like 100% completion, 250 stunts and the shooting range golds. Save A Long Road for last, since reaching 100% completion naturally clears most of the remaining requirements along the way. Expect a long road: a full platinum run takes most players well over 60 hours. Keep a checklist as you go, because the collectible and activity trophies are the easiest to leave half-finished and forget.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission of GTA VI, so this trophy is unmissable and pops within your first hour in Leonida. Play through the introduction as Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, follow the on-screen prompts, and finish the mission's objectives — driving, a short on-foot section and the scripted beats that set up the story. There is nothing to prepare and no way to fail permanently: if you die or fail an objective, simply retry from the checkpoint and continue. Treat it as the game's way of welcoming you to Vice City. Once the mission-complete screen appears, the trophy unlocks immediately.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Play through every mission in Chapter 1 of the story and this trophy unlocks when the chapter's final mission ends. Chapters in GTA VI follow Lucia and Jason as their plan unravels across Leonida, starting around Vice City and the surrounding towns. There is no optional requirement: just complete the story missions in order, using checkpoints to retry anything you fail. If you are unsure whether a mission belongs to Chapter 1, the in-game mission log shows your current chapter. This is an unmissable story trophy, so it will come naturally on any playthrough — no side content, collectibles or special conditions are needed.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2 and the trophy pops as the chapter closes. The second chapter pushes Lucia and Jason deeper into Leonida's criminal world, with bigger jobs and new contacts across Vice City. Like all chapter trophies, this one is unmissable: simply play the story in order and it will unlock on its own. If a mission gives you trouble, use cover, stock up on ammo and armour before starting, and retry from checkpoints — failed attempts never lock you out. You do not need to complete any side activities, stranger missions or collectibles for this trophy, so you can focus purely on the main story if you want.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete all of Chapter 3's story missions to unlock this trophy. By this point in the game you are firmly established in Vice City itself, and the missions grow more ambitious, mixing driving, shooting and set-piece moments across the city and its outskirts. This is another unmissable story trophy: play the missions in order and it pops when the chapter ends. There are no hidden requirements, no collectibles to find and no difficulty setting to worry about — story trophies unlock on any difficulty. If you want to break up the story, Chapter 3 is a good time to try side activities, since much of the map is open by now.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish the final chapter's missions and this trophy unlocks as Chapter 4 closes, leaving only the finale ahead. The fourth chapter is the endgame of the story, so expect tougher shootouts and longer missions — bring full armour, a good weapon loadout and a fast car before starting each one. As with the earlier chapters, this trophy is unmissable and unlocks on any difficulty just by completing the story missions in order. You do not need 100% completion or any side content. Once it pops, you are one step from the gold trophy for finishing the game, so keep pushing through the final mission.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: This gold trophy unlocks when you complete the final story mission of GTA VI, closing out Lucia and Jason's story. It is unmissable: reach the end of Chapter 4 and finish the last mission, whatever choices you made along the way. The finale is typically the hardest mission in the game, so prepare properly — full health and armour, your best weapons with plenty of ammo, and ideally a save made before you start so you can retry cleanly. Use cover, take the fight slowly, and lean on your partner during co-op-style sections. When the credits roll, the trophy pops. Note that finishing the story is only the start: the platinum still needs the side content.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run and this trophy unlocks. Named missions like this one appear in the story as you progress through the chapters, and the trophy pops as soon as the mission-complete screen shows. There is nothing special to do beyond finishing the mission's objectives — follow the waypoint, complete each beat, and use checkpoints if you fail a section. This is an unmissable story trophy, so it will come naturally during a normal playthrough. If you are trophy hunting efficiently, do not worry about it: just keep playing the story and check it off when it appears.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. This is one of the game's big set-piece heists, so expect a multi-stage mission with planning, a build-up and a high-stakes payoff against cartel opposition. Stock up on armour and ammo beforehand, keep a fast getaway vehicle in mind, and use cover during the shootouts — heist missions punish reckless rushing. The trophy is unmissable and unlocks the moment the mission completes, on any difficulty. If you fail, checkpoints let you retry the failed section without replaying the whole mission. No side content or collectibles are required for this trophy.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. This mission appears in the story flow, and the trophy unlocks as soon as you see the mission-complete screen. Play through its objectives in order, following the waypoints and completing each scripted beat. As with every named story-mission trophy, it is unmissable: there is no optional objective or special condition, and it unlocks on any difficulty. If a section trips you up, retry from the checkpoint and adjust your approach — slower, more careful play with cover usually beats sprinting through. Nothing outside the story is needed, so just keep playing.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. This is another named mission in the main story, and the trophy pops automatically when the mission ends. Follow the objectives through, use checkpoints to recover from any failed section, and do not worry about optional goals — the trophy only cares that the mission is complete. It is unmissable on any difficulty and needs no side content. If you are tracking your progress, note that named-mission trophies like this one are simply milestones along the story, so the best approach is to play the campaign in order and let them unlock naturally as you go.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. Expect an airport infiltration with tight corridors, armed opposition and a vehicle-based escape — bring armour, a reliable automatic weapon and plenty of ammo. The trophy is unmissable and unlocks when the mission completes, on any difficulty. Use cover, move between checkpoints carefully, and retry failed sections from the checkpoint rather than restarting the whole mission. No collectibles or side activities are required. Once the mission-complete screen appears, the trophy is yours and you can continue the story.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. Despite the name, this is a story mission in sunny Leonida rather than a weather event — the title is the operation's codename. Expect a large, combat-heavy mission with multiple stages, so go in prepared with full armour, strong weapons and a plan for the escape. The trophy is unmissable and pops when the mission-complete screen shows, on any difficulty. If you fail a section, the checkpoint system lets you retry just that part. No side content is needed; simply play the story in order and this trophy will unlock naturally.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the in-game completion checklist — the single biggest task in the game and the second gold trophy. The checklist covers story missions, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and assorted side objectives across Leonida; open the stats or checklist screen to see exactly what is still missing. Work through it methodically and save this trophy for last, since most other trophies feed into it. The long grinds are the 250 stunts, the shooting range golds, the card sets and the 100 WAiNK locations, so chip away at those during the story rather than leaving them all for the end. Expect 30 to 40 hours beyond the main story.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts across Leonida — jumps, near misses, long airtime, drifts and other driving feats that the game counts as a stunt. The counter ticks up during normal play, especially if you drive fast, take ramps and use the map's many jumps, but 250 is a real grind, so treat it as a background task. A good farming method is to find a reliable ramp or jump, hit it repeatedly, and let the counter climb; stunt jumps marked on the map are the most consistent. Use a fast, durable car and avoid traffic-heavy areas when farming. Check your stats screen to track the count, and expect several hours of deliberate effort if you chase it all at once.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every activity type in the game at least once. GTA VI packs Leonida with pastimes — racing, fishing, shooting range challenges, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation and more — and this trophy simply asks you to sample each one. You do not need to win, score well or finish anything: starting and completing a single session of each type is enough. Work through them one by one in free roam after the story opens the map up, using the in-game activity markers and your phone to find venues. Keep a mental checklist, and if the trophy has not popped, revisit the activities you have only watched or walked past without playing.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Head to a shooting range — Ammu-Nation ranges are the usual venue — and work through the challenge list weapon by weapon. Gold medals demand accuracy and speed, so learn each challenge's target pattern before going for a serious run, and use the weapon the challenge specifies rather than your favourite. Take your time on the first attempt to memorise the layout, then push for gold once you know where targets appear. This is one of the harder silver trophies: expect several hours, and do the easier challenges first to build confidence and unlock the trickier ones.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations across Leonida. Drone races are found at Top Fun sites marked on the map; fly the course through the checkpoints as fast as you can, cutting corners where the gates allow it. The drone handles differently from a car, so spend your first run learning the course, then go for the win on the second. Some locations are trickier than others — tight turns and low gates punish sloppy flying — so retry freely, since attempts are quick. You do not need to win every race type at a location, just one win per location, and the trophy pops after the fourteenth.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races across Leonida — street races, off-road events and any other race type the game offers. Races are found through markers around the map and your phone; each distinct race counts once, so you need 20 separate events, not 20 wins of the same one. Pick a fast, well-handling car, learn the route on your first attempt, and use slipstreaming and clean cornering to pull ahead. Some races are easier in a tuned vehicle, so invest in upgrades if you are struggling. The trophy pops on your twentieth distinct win. It pairs naturally with exploring the map, since race markers are scattered all over the state.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a fishing rival you meet through the game's fishing activity — head to a fishing spot, start a challenge against him, and out-fish him. Fishing in GTA VI is a timing and patience game: cast, wait for the bite, then reel steadily without letting the line snap, keeping tension in the safe zone. Watch Cal's score and aim to land bigger or more numerous catches than he does. If you lose, you can retry the challenge as often as you like. Bring the best rod and bait you can buy, fish calm waters, and do not rush the reel when a big fish fights back.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete any single arcade game in Leonida. Arcade machines are found in bars, arcades and other venues around Vice City — walk up to one, pay the small fee if required, and play the game through to its end. You do not need a high score or a perfect run; simply finishing the game is enough, so pick the shortest or easiest cabinet you can find. If you fail or run out of lives, retry — attempts are cheap and quick. This is one of the easiest trophies in the set and a nice palate cleanser between story missions, so grab it whenever you pass an arcade machine in free roam.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's stranger mission strand, ending with his final mission. Stranger missions appear as question-mark markers on the map once you meet the character; work through Andy's strand in order and the trophy pops when the last mission completes. Stranger strands can be easy to miss if you never visit their part of the map, so check for new markers after each story chapter and clear them as they appear. The missions themselves are usually short — a drive, a conversation, a small job — and they are unmissable in the sense that they stay available in free roam. Finish the final one and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's stranger mission strand through to its final mission. The title hints at boats, so expect at least part of Kenton's story to take place on the water around Leonida's coast and waterways — bring a boat or be ready to commandeer one. Find Kenton's marker on the map, play each mission in his strand in order, and the trophy unlocks when the last one ends. Stranger strands stay available in free roam, so there is no rush and no way to miss them by progressing the story. Clear the marker whenever it appears and work through the strand steadily.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's stranger mission strand, finishing with his final mission. The name suggests a biker, so expect motorcycles and open-road riding to feature in his missions — a fast bike and decent riding skills will help. Track Billy's marker on the map, complete each mission in the strand in order, and the trophy pops when the final mission ends. Like other stranger strands, Billy's stays available in free roam and does not expire, so you can do it at your own pace after the story. If the marker is not showing, progress the story a little further, since some strands only unlock in later chapters.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands across Leonida. Strangers appear as question-mark markers on the map; each one is a short chain of missions for a colourful local character, and a strand counts once its final mission is done. Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have their own strand, and three more strangers are waiting elsewhere in the state. Work through them as their markers appear — new strands unlock as the story progresses, so keep checking the map after each chapter. The trophy pops when your eighth strand is complete. This is a silver because it takes time and exploration, but none of the individual missions are hard.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's stranger mission strand, ending with his final mission. The title points to supply runs, so expect delivery-style jobs — moving goods across Leonida, possibly under time pressure or with rivals in pursuit. Find Randy's marker, play through his strand in order, and the trophy unlocks when the last mission completes. Stranger strands remain available in free roam, so there is no deadline and no way to miss this by advancing the story. Use a fast, sturdy vehicle for the delivery missions and keep an eye on the map for Randy's marker after each story chapter.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's stranger mission strand, finishing with his final mission. The title suggests music or DJ culture, so expect Tyrone's strand to involve Vice City's nightlife scene. Find his marker on the map, work through the strand's missions in order, and the trophy pops when the final one ends. Stranger strands do not expire and stay available in free roam, so play them at your own pace — but do not leave them all until after the story, since new strands unlock gradually and it is easy to forget a marker in a far corner of the map. Clear Tyrone's strand as soon as his missions appear.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots scattered across Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet, scenic locations — beaches, hilltops, parks and other peaceful corners of the state — where you can sit and meditate for a short scene. You do not need to do anything difficult: visit the spot, start the meditation, and let it finish. The challenge is finding all 18, since they are spread across the whole map, including rural areas far from Vice City. Use a map or checklist to track the ones you have visited, and combine the hunt with exploring the state for other trophies. The trophy pops after the eighteenth meditation.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret, one of Leonida's stranger characters. Bret's strand involves tracking a specific rare animal — follow his missions until he points you at the target, then hunt it down in the wilds of Leonida. Use a scoped rifle for a clean shot at range, move slowly and watch the wind and your surroundings so you do not spook the animal. The animal's exact location and species are revealed through Bret's missions, so do not go wandering the swamps blind: play the strand first and let it guide you. Once the hunt is complete and you return to Bret, the trophy unlocks.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets. Cards are hidden throughout Leonida — tucked into shops, bars, back rooms and other tucked-away spots — and each set needs every card in it. This is a scavenger hunt: explore thoroughly, check interiors as well as streets, and use a checklist or map to track which cards you still need. You only need 3 sets, not every card in the game, so focus on the sets you are closest to finishing. Cards can also sometimes be bought or traded, so check in-game shops and your phone for options. The trophy pops the moment your third set is complete.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It feature at 100 different locations across Leonida. WAiNK is the game's in-world social photo or check-in feature — open it at a location, capture the moment, and the spot counts toward your total. The 100 locations are spread all over the state, so treat this as a long exploration task: hit WAiNK spots whenever you pass a landmark, viewpoint or notable place, and use a checklist to track which areas you have covered. You do not need to do anything difficult at each spot, just use the feature once there. The trophy pops after the hundredth location, and it pairs well with the exploration trophy.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's assorted side objectives — feats of driving, shooting, exploration and general mayhem tracked in your stats, from stunt jumps to weapon feats and more. The counter climbs naturally as you play, especially if you vary what you do instead of sticking to one activity. Check the challenges list in the pause menu to see what is available and what you are close to finishing, then pick off the easy ones first. You do not need to complete every challenge in the game, just 50 of them. The trophy pops once your fiftieth challenge is done, and it usually arrives during a normal platinum run.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner — Lucia or Jason, whichever you are not playing — build up a 4-star wanted level together, then lose the cops and escape. The easiest way is to commit crimes in free roam with your partner alongside you until the wanted level hits 4 stars, then break line of sight and hide until the stars clear. Use alleys, tunnels and the countryside to lose pursuing units, and switch vehicles if yours is too hot. Avoid the airport and police-heavy areas while escaping. The trophy pops the moment the wanted level fully clears with your partner still with you. If your partner gets lost or arrested, regroup and try again.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, rob 3 shops in a row without letting your wanted level drop — the streak only counts while the heat stays on. Pick three shops close together in Vice City so you can move between them quickly, and keep your partner with you throughout. Enter, threaten the clerk, grab the cash, and get straight to the next shop before the wanted level fades. The tricky part is keeping the wanted level alive while moving: do not hide or wait too long between robberies, and do not get arrested. Plan the route first, use a fast car, and the trophy pops after the third shop in the streak.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles across Leonida. A vehicle counts as discovered when you first get in and drive it — or when the game registers it in your vehicle collection — so variety is the goal. Cruise the streets of Vice City, visit car parks, dealerships and rural areas, and jump into anything you have not driven before: cars, bikes, trucks, boats and aircraft all count toward the total. The counter climbs fast if you deliberately try new vehicles instead of sticking to one favourite. Check your stats or collection screen to see your progress. The trophy pops at 100 distinct vehicles discovered.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single use of Combat Focus, GTA VI's slow-motion aiming mode. Find a spot with plenty of enemies — a gang hideout, a police shootout or a mission with waves of attackers — and wait until at least five are in view before activating Combat Focus. Aim for headshots to drop them fast, and keep moving between targets rather than lingering on one. The key is timing: trigger Combat Focus only when you can see five enemies at once, since the meter runs out quickly. If you fall short, retry in another busy firefight. Missions with large enemy groups are the most reliable place to attempt it.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from Vice City International Airport — in plain terms, steal a plane and take off without following the rules. Head to VCIA, get onto the airfield, climb into a parked aircraft and take off down the runway. Expect airport security and possibly police attention, so move fast once you are on the tarmac. Any flyable plane should work; smaller aircraft are easier to get airborne quickly. The trophy pops once you are in the air and clear of the airport. If you get stopped on the runway, retry — the airport is open in free roam, so you can attempt this as often as you like.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: This trophy involves the Rhino tank, and the description's joke — 'kinda hot in these Rhinos' — suggests getting inside one or surviving around them. Rhinos appear when your wanted level is very high, typically at 5 or 6 stars, or at military locations. The official description does not spell out the exact trigger, so treat this as a high-wanted-level activity: max out the heat, wait for a Rhino to arrive, and engage with it. Be ready for a heavy police response, and flag this one as uncertain until the community pins down the precise trigger.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a stealth job, not a smash-and-grab. Find a jewelry store in Vice City, case it first, and go in quietly: avoid the clerk's line of sight, move slowly, and take the goods without triggering an alarm or alerting anyone. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so retreat and try again rather than fighting your way out. The exact stealth mechanics are not spelled out in the official description, so expect to use crouching, timing and patience — strike when the store is quiet and the clerk is distracted. The trophy pops once you leave with the loot undetected.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults across Leonida and escape cleanly after each one. Bank vault robberies are major undertakings: plan the approach, crack or breach the vault, grab the cash, and then lose the police before the trophy counts the job. Each vault is a separate event, so you will need to find and hit five of them — they are spread around the state, and some may only become available as the story progresses. Bring armour and a fast getaway car, and plan your escape route before you go in. The trophy pops after your fifth successful vault robbery and escape.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape with the cash. Armored trucks drive set routes around Vice City and Leonida — watch for them on the road, then stop the truck by blocking it, ramming it or shooting out its tyres. Once it is stopped, breach the rear doors, grab the money, and lose the police that respond. A fast car and a planned escape route help a lot: head for alleys or the countryside to break line of sight. The trophy pops once you escape with the wanted level cleared. If the truck gets away or you get caught, look for another one — they spawn regularly in free roam.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore every area of Leonida — all 52 named areas, from the streets of Vice City to the swamps, beaches, small towns and countryside in between. An area counts once you have visited it, so the method is simple: drive, fly or sail across the whole map and let the counter climb. Use the in-game map to spot regions you have not entered yet, and work through them systematically — a helicopter or plane makes the far corners much faster to reach. This trophy pairs naturally with the WAiNK, meditation and vehicle trophies, so combine the trips. The trophy pops when the last unexplored area is visited.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs operating in Leonida. Gangs control drug labs, stash houses and other illicit businesses around the state — find one operation per gang, hit it, take the goods or cash, and get out. Gang operations are usually marked or discoverable through exploration and story contacts, and each gang's territory is distinct, so you will travel all over the map. Expect armed resistance at every site, so go in with armour and a good weapon. The trophy pops once you have robbed an operation for all 9 gangs. Keep notes on which gangs you have done, since it is easy to hit the same gang twice.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Head to Ocean Beach in Vice City, find a beachfront bar or cocktail spot with a view of the water, and enjoy a cocktail there. This is a relaxed, scenic trophy: order a drink at a beachside venue and take in the view. Ocean Beach is the famous strip along the Vice City waterfront, so look for bars and cafes facing the ocean. The trophy should pop once the drinking scene or interaction completes. If one venue does not trigger it, try another spot along the beachfront. There is no time pressure and no skill involved — it is one of the easiest trophies in the game, and a good one to grab early.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic GTA style — drive a car straight through the showroom's glass frontage and out onto the street. Find a vehicle showroom in Vice City, get inside with a car, then accelerate through the windows in a shower of glass. This is a deliberate homage to the series' classic moments, and the trophy should pop as soon as you break out through the glass. Any car will do, but a fast one makes the exit more dramatic. Expect a wanted level for the property damage, so be ready to drive away quickly. If the first attempt does not trigger it, try a different showroom.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley in Vice City and play a game of bowling, following through on the shot. This is a nod to the series' past — bowling was a classic pastime in GTA IV — and the trophy asks you to simply play at this specific alley. Walk in, start a game, and complete a frame or two; you do not need a strike or a high score, just a proper follow-through on your throws. The alley is a named location, so look for it on the map or ask around in-game. The trophy pops once you have bowled at Kolt & Associates. It is quick, easy and a fun piece of series history.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This trophy is tied to Lucia and Jason's partnership reaching a moment of mass appeal — a story or relationship milestone whose exact trigger is not spelled out in the official description. It most likely unlocks through a specific story scene or a partner activity where the duo's fame or public profile peaks. Play through the story and keep an eye on partner activities and social-media-style moments in the game; the trophy should come naturally as the campaign progresses. Do not go hunting for a specific activity for this one — just play the story and check it off when it pops.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices throughout the story — this trophy tracks the decisions Lucia and Jason make, for better or worse. GTA VI presents choice moments in missions and conversations, and this trophy appears to count them up over a playthrough. The honest position is that the official description does not state a number or a specific choice, so the trigger is uncertain; community tracking suggests a substantial count of decisions is involved. Play the story naturally, engage with dialogue options and mission choices when they appear, and do not skip cutscenes that offer a decision. This is the one trophy flagged as potentially missable if a playthrough skips too many choice moments.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Succeed on your second try at something — that is what the description implies. This is likely tied to retrying a failed attempt, whether a mission, a challenge or an activity, and succeeding the second time around. The most reliable approach is to fail a short activity or mission section once, then complete it on the immediate retry. Because the official description is vague, the exact trigger is uncertain, and this trophy is flagged as such — do not grind for it specifically. Play normally, and if you fail something and then succeed on the next attempt, it may pop on its own. If it has not appeared by the end of the story, retry a quick activity deliberately.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange — this is GTA VI's mystery or easter-egg trophy. The description gives nothing away, which is the point: somewhere in Leonida there is a bizarre event, sighting or encounter, and this trophy pops when you see it. Likely candidates are the series' classic weirdness: a UFO, a cryptid in the swamps, or a strange late-night event in a remote corner of the map. Explore unusual locations at odd hours, especially the swamps and deserted areas, and keep an eye out for anything out of place. The exact trigger is uncertain from the official description alone, so this one is flagged as such.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — attack a pedestrian from a moving vehicle using a melee weapon. Get in a car or on a bike, equip a melee weapon such as a bat, and drive past a pedestrian while swinging. Timing is the trick: slow down enough to connect, but keep moving so it counts as a drive-by. Quiet streets with lone pedestrians are the best place to try, and the beachfront or side streets of Vice City work well. If your first swings miss, keep trying — the hitbox is forgiving once you get the rhythm. The trophy pops the moment a pedestrian goes down to your melee drive-by.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty cash earned from heists and robberies that cannot be spent directly — you need to clean them through your contacts, who take a cut and return usable money. Find your laundering contacts through the story and your phone, hand over Marked Bills in batches, and keep going until $250,000 has been cleaned. The total accumulates over the whole playthrough, so launder regularly instead of hoarding bills. Heists and bank vaults are the best source of Marked Bills, so this trophy pairs naturally with the robbery trophies. It pops once the $250,000 threshold is reached.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops in Leonida. The counter tracks total spending at every shop type — clothes, weapons, car modifications, food, and anything else you can buy — so it climbs naturally as you play. The fastest way to reach $100,000 is to invest in things you actually need: a good weapon loadout, car upgrades, and a solid wardrobe all add up quickly. Expensive cars and high-end clothes are the quickest single purchases if you want to finish it deliberately. Check your stats screen to track total spending. The trophy pops once your cumulative spending crosses $100,000, and most players reach it during a normal playthrough.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties across Leonida. Garages are buyable properties that let you store vehicles — look for For Sale signs and property markers on the map, or check the in-game property listings on your phone. Each garage costs money, so this trophy is partly a savings goal: story payouts, heists and laundering Marked Bills will fund it. Buy them as you can afford them rather than saving up for all eight at once, and remember that garages also help with the vehicle trophies, since stored cars stay available. The trophy pops when the eighth and final garage property is purchased.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app on your in-game phone. Scooter Bros is the game's vehicle delivery and registration service: drive a vehicle you want to keep, open the app, and register it so you can call it up later. Any vehicle type should count, so register the cars and bikes you actually use as you find them — there is no need to hunt for rare vehicles, just register ten different ones over the course of play. Stolen cars, purchased cars and mission vehicles all work. The trophy pops once the tenth vehicle is registered. It is a quick, easy trophy that rewards using the app naturally.
